name: Jagelon Guard – Technical SEO & Site Monitoring
author: securplan

sections.description:
Jagelon Guard gives every site owner a free, one-click SEO Health Check. It reads
the public home page, robots.txt and XML sitemap, then explains what is correct,
what needs attention and what could not be checked. The audit is read-only, works
without an account or key and does not send site data to Jagelon.

The plugin also keeps the technical foundations of SEO in order locally inside
WordPress. An optional monitoring service checks the public site every 15 minutes
and warns you when a quiet change could cost visibility or traffic.

Free technical SEO — no account required

  • a one-click, read-only SEO Health Check for the home page, robots.txt,
    XML sitemap, HTTPS, metadata, Open Graph, JSON-LD and the main H1 heading
  • an SEO panel in the editor of every page and post: title and description in
    Google with a live preview and character counter, and a “hide from Google” switch
  • home page title and description, with the same preview
  • company details for search engines and AI assistants: business type, phone,
    email, address and profiles (Google Business Profile, Facebook, LinkedIn),
    published as Organization or LocalBusiness structured data
  • canonical links, with WordPress core’s own tag replaced by one you control
  • the native WordPress sitemap, without author pages
  • robots.txt rules
  • Open Graph tags
  • Organization and WebSite schema (JSON-LD)
  • a clean settings screen with tabs, a status overview and a logo picker from
    the media library
  • an optional “business card site” mode for sites without a blog: category,
    tag and author archives and RSS feeds are hidden

These features run on your own site, do not expire and need no connection key.

Optional monitoring every 15 minutes

Sites rarely break loudly. An update quietly sets noindex, someone edits a
page title that used to rank, a redirect behind a paid ad starts returning 404.
The site still looks fine in a browser, so nobody notices for weeks.

The optional Jagelon Guard service checks your public site every 15 minutes and
tells you what changed, where it happened, how long it has lasted and what to
check next:

  • an event log in your WordPress dashboard
  • a weekly email report, including the quiet weeks
  • recommendations ranked by importance, each listing the affected addresses

The monitoring service observes and advises. Nothing on your site changes on its own:
in the paid plan, fixes proposed by the site audit are applied only after you
approve them in WordPress, and every one can be rolled back with one click.

Jagelon Guard reports, the event log and recommendations are currently written in
Polish. The free features above are fully available in English.

How to get the monitoring service

The monitoring service is a paid subscription, billed yearly, with no account
needed before you buy. After payment you receive a connection key by email and
paste it into the plugin. Details and current pricing:
https://securplan.pl/en/jagelon-guard/

Everything described above under free features stays free and needs no key.

Privacy and resilience

Connecting is optional. Without a connection every local feature listed above
keeps working.

What the plugin sends to the service, and only after you paste a connection key:

  • your site address
  • WordPress, PHP and plugin versions
  • the results of the service’s own checks of your public pages
  • a timestamp for each connection

It does not send post content, user data, database contents or anything from
inside wp-admin. If the service is unavailable, the local SEO features keep
working. Only monitoring and reports pause.

Service terms: https://securplan.pl/regulamin/
Privacy policy: https://securplan.pl/polityka-prywatnosci/
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Jagelon Guard in the main admin menu.
  3. Fill in the metadata fields. That is all the free part needs.
  4. The optional monitoring service is a paid subscription; after buying it at
    https://securplan.pl/en/jagelon-guard/ you receive a connection key by e-mail.
    Paste it under Connection. The free features above need no key.
sections.faq:
Does the free plugin work without an account or key?

Yes. Titles, descriptions, canonicals, the sitemap, robots.txt, Open Graph and
schema run locally and do not expire. The manual SEO Health Check is also fully
available without registration or a connection to the monitoring service.

What does the free SEO Health Check inspect?

It checks whether the public home page can be loaded and reviews its title, meta
description, canonical URL, indexing directives, Open Graph tags, JSON-LD and H1.
It also checks robots.txt, the XML sitemap, HTTPS and redirects. The audit is
read-only and never edits content or settings.

Why does a check sometimes say “Could not check”?

Some hosting providers block a site’s own loopback HTTP requests. Jagelon Guard
reports those tests as unavailable instead of presenting a false SEO error. No
setting is weakened and no remote service receives the page data.

What does the optional monitoring service check?

It checks the public site every 15 minutes for high-impact changes such as
noindex, robots.txt changes, missing or foreign canonicals, changed titles,
sitemap failures and HTTP errors.

Does Jagelon Guard change or repair my site?

Not on its own. The free plugin and the monitoring service observe, record and
recommend. In the paid plan the site audit can propose fixes (for example
missing company details); they are applied only after you approve them in
WordPress, checked on the live page and can be rolled back with one click.

Will it fight my other SEO plugin?

No. When Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework,
Slim SEO or Squirrly SEO is active, Jagelon Guard does not add duplicate SEO
output. Optional monitoring can continue alongside the other plugin.

What data is sent to the monitoring service?

Only the site address, WordPress/PHP/plugin versions, results of checks of public
pages and connection timestamps, and only after a connection key is entered. No
post content, user data, database contents or wp-admin data is sent.

What happens if the service is unavailable?

The local SEO features remain active. Monitoring and reports pause until the
service is available again.
sections.changelog:
0.13.4

Everything new in the free plugin since 0.10.0:
* New look for the settings screen: tabs, a status overview at the top and
clearer forms. Works the same without JavaScript.
* New “Company details” tab: business type (Organization or LocalBusiness),
description, phone, email, address and company profiles, added to the home
page structured data that search engines and AI assistants use to recognise
the company. Includes a logo picker from the media library.
* “Check status” button refreshes the connection to the monitoring service on
demand, and a “Settings saved” message after saving.
* SEO Health Check: translator notes for every message with a number or
address, so translations read correctly.

Paid Jagelon Guard plan only (not part of this plugin package): fixes proposed
by the site audit and applied after your approval, notifications about new
fixes, and the Discovery timeline of how changed pages reach search engines.

0.10.1

  • The weekly report no longer calls a one-off change an ongoing problem. A
    changed title, heading, canonical, robots.txt or sitemap now says when it was
    noticed; genuine faults still say how long they have been going on and are
    listed first.
  • The report explains that confirming a change in the panel stops the reminder,
    so the same line no longer returns week after week.
  • Settings and the site pairing survive the rename from Securplan SEO Core.

0.10.0

  • Adds the free, manual SEO Health Check. It works without an account, changes
    no site settings and clearly separates correct, warning, error and unavailable
    results.
  • The check remains available alongside Yoast SEO, Rank Math and All in One SEO,
    without producing duplicate metadata.
  • Adds same-site request restrictions, nonce and capability checks, a short
    per-user rate limit, responsive results and deterministic regression tests.

0.9.30

  • The plugin is now Jagelon Guard. The previous name could be confused with
    an unrelated trademark, so the plugin, its text domain and its admin screen
    were renamed.
  • The character counter label is JSON-encoded with escaped angle brackets, so
    a translation cannot break out of the inline script.

0.9.29

  • Admin styles and scripts are loaded through the WordPress enqueue API.
  • Structured data (JSON-LD) escapes HTML tags, so no site value can close the
    script element.
  • Translations are delivered through translate.wordpress.org; the package no
    longer bundles language files.

0.9.28

  • Build fix: the paid package is buildable again. The update channel was
    dropped from the whole source tree instead of only from the directory
    build, so paid sites shipped since 0.9.18 could no longer update
    themselves. The directory package is unchanged: it carries no update
    channel and no Fix module.

0.9.27

  • Ready for the Jagelon Guard trial: the expiry reminder counts down 3 days and
    1 day for a trial (30 and 7 days for a yearly plan), and the event log stays
    visible after monitoring stops.

0.9.26

  • Screenshots and listing graphics for the plugin directory.

0.9.25

  • The settings screen is now fully translatable. The indexing section mixed
    an English heading with Polish labels, and the event log and
    recommendations headings stayed Polish on every site, connected or not.

0.9.23

  • “Tested up to” is declared only in the readme, where the directory expects
    it, so the two cannot drift apart.

0.9.22

  • Plugin URI now points at the plugin’s own page, separate from the author
    URI, as the directory requires.

0.9.21

  • The request URI is unslashed and sanitised before use, as recommended by
    Plugin Check.

0.9.20

  • The SEO panel keeps a readable width after being moved out of the editor
    sidebar with the “move up” arrow.

0.9.19

  • A site set to “Discourage search engines” no longer serves a working XML
    sitemap, and robots.txt no longer advertises one. Staging copies could be
    found and indexed despite the setting.

0.9.18

  • Jetpack no longer adds a second set of Open Graph tags next to ours.

0.9.17

  • SEO panel in the page and post editor: title, description, live Google
    preview and a “hide from Google” switch.
  • Steps back automatically when another SEO plugin is active.
  • Hiding category, tag and author archives and RSS feeds is now an opt-in
    “business card site” setting, and blog posts stay in the sitemap. Sites
    updated from an earlier version keep their previous behaviour.
  • Home page metadata fields explain their defaults, with a Google preview and
    a character counter.
  • The monitoring service is now consistently called Jagelon Guard.
  • The settings screen now starts with what already works, a next step and
    what Jagelon Guard adds, instead of unavailable modules.
  • A fresh install no longer reports a lost connection it never had.
  • Removed the plugin author’s product and e-mail address from the structured
    data (schema) added to every site.

0.9.16

  • Comments and pingbacks are no longer switched off without asking. The
    setting is off by default.
  • English is now the source language; Polish ships as a translation.
  • The paid Fix module is no longer part of this package.

0.9.15

  • Event log shows the previous and current value of what changed.

0.9.14

  • Recommendations list the affected addresses instead of only counting them,
    with a link straight to the editor.

screenshots.caption:
The overview, the moment the plugin is activated: what already works on
your site — sitemap, robots.txt, canonical addresses, social previews and
organisation data. No account, no key, no setup.

Home page title and description, with a live preview of how the page
looks in Google results and a character counter for each field.

Company details for search engines and AI assistants: business type,
contact details, address and profiles, with a logo picker from the media
library.

Indexing and technical SEO settings, each with a plain-language note on
what it changes and when to leave it alone.

The free SEO Health Check showing a real read-only audit, clear result counts
and practical explanations for correct items and warnings.

See exactly how a page will look in Google before you publish it:
title, description, a live preview and a character count that tells
you when you have said enough. A switch hides a single page from
Google, for pages such as "thank you for your order".
